Mission Local’s four data takeaways were:

- Turnout was 78.9%—below the 86.3% recorded in 2020 and only slightly above the long-term average for presidential elections. About 412,000 people voted, 38,000 fewer than in 2020.
- Geography shaped results, especially on Proposition K: voters in districts near the Great Highway opposed closing it, but the measure passed citywide, 55–45. District-level voting also showed divides in supervisor races.
- At least $72 million was spent across the election. Daniel Lurie’s mayoral campaign spent $16 million; Proposition D raised $9.5 million and lost, while Proposition E raised $69,159 and passed.
- Redistricting affected district races beyond Districts 5 and 7: new Seacliff precincts in District 1 favored Marjan Philhour, while new Russian Hill precincts helped Danny Sauter in District 3.
